title: Bitwise XOR Parity Property Solution for We Need the Zero
approach_explanation:
The problem asks if we can find an integer $x$ such that XOR-ing every element in array $a$ with $x$ yields an overall XOR sum of $0$. Let $S =  igoplus_{i=1}^n a_i$. When we XOR each element $a_i$ with $x$, the new array elements are $b_i = a_i  igoplus x$. The XOR sum of the new array $b$ is: $B =  igoplus_{i=1}^n (a_i  igoplus x)$. Due to the associativity and commutativity of the XOR operation, if $n$ is even, $x$ appears an even number of times, so $B = S  igoplus (x  igoplus x  igoplus 	ext{...}) = S  igoplus 0 = S$. Thus, if $n$ is even, $B = 0$ requires $S = 0$. If $S 
eq 0$, no such $x$ exists (output -1), and if $S = 0$, any $x$ (like 0) works. If $n$ is odd, $x$ appears an odd number of times, so $B = S  igoplus x$. To make $B = 0$, we need $S  igoplus x = 0$, which gives $x = S$. Thus, for odd $n$, the answer is always $S$.

code_breakdown.section_title: Test Case Initialization and XOR Sum Accumulation
code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$, then loops $t$ times. For each test case, reads the array length $n$ and computes the total XOR sum (`xor_sum`) of all elements in array $a$.
Checks if $n$ is even or odd. If $n$ is even, outputs $0$ if `xor_sum` is $0$, and $-1$ otherwise. If $n$ is odd, directly outputs the `xor_sum` as the required value of $x$.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each test case, we iterate through the array of size $n$ once to compute the bitwise XOR sum. Summing over all test cases, the total time complexity is $O(\sum n)$, which is bounded by $O(10^3)$ operations, comfortably passing within the 1-second time limit.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: The algorithm processes the array elements on-the-fly without storing them in a vector or array. Only a few primitive integer variables (`t`, `n`, `xor_sum`, `x`) are maintained, resulting in constant extra memory.

strengths: Clean, concise implementation avoiding unnecessary array storage.
Correctly handles the parity cases derived from the mathematical properties of XOR.
edge_cases_handled: Arrays where elements are already yielding a zero XOR sum.
Arrays of even length with non-zero initial XOR sums (correctly returns -1).
